references.text: The text deals with promises made with one's lips and the consequences of failing to keep them, reflecting the principle that it is better not to make a vow than to break it.
Describes the obligation to fulfill vows and oaths sworn to the Lord, contrasting with the freedom to choose not to make a vow in the first place.
The Preacher emphasizes that it is better not to make a vow than to make one and fail to keep it, directly supporting the message of Deuteronomy 23:23.
Warns against hastily dedicating something to the Lord and then regretting the vow, highlighting the importance of thinking carefully before making promises.
Jesus teaches about keeping one's oaths and vows, urging honesty in speech without the need to swear, reflecting the principle of accountability in commitments.
